as_written_in_papers.quote: Homozygous of two novel “likely pathogenic” missense variants, c.920T>C (p.Leu307Pro) in exon 8 and c.758G>A (p.Arg253His) in exon 7, and homozygous of a novel nonsense mutation, c.262C>T (p.Gln88Ter) in exon 4 of the ITGB2 gene were identified in the genomic DNA of P1 and P2, respectively.
The results revealed two novel homozygous missense mutations, c.920C>T (p.Leu307Pro) in exon 8 and c.758G>A (p.Arg253His) in exon 7
The reference sequences were NM_000211.5 and NP_000202.3 for ITGB2 cDNA and β2 integrin amino acid positions, respectively.

cases.statement: One person: P1 (Case 1), a Burmese boy, homozygous for c.920T>C together with a second homozygous ITGB2 variant c.758G>A (p.Arg253His).

Case 1: A 21-mo-old Burmese boy presented with prolonged fever and multiple whitish ulcers in the oropharynx (Patient #1, P1).
Case 1: The patient had a delayed umbilical cord detachment 30 d after birth and delayed wound healing, resulting in difficult-to-treat omphalitis.
Case 1: Complete blood count revealed leukocytosis (WBC 94600/mm^3) and neutrophil predominance (67166/mm^3), while anti-HIV was negative.
He was re-admitted several times with chronic wound infections around the tracheostomy site, Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia, oral candidiasis, and cellulitis.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Classic early-onset features (delayed cord detachment at 30 days, omphalitis, soft-tissue infections, delayed wound healing, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis). Anti-HIV negative and bone marrow without malignancy; CD18 flow cytometry not done; no other genes tested.

quotes.quote: Case 1: The patient had a delayed umbilical cord detachment 30 d after birth and delayed wound healing, resulting in difficult-to-treat omphalitis.
Case 1: Complete blood count revealed leukocytosis (WBC 94600/mm^3) and neutrophil predominance (67166/mm^3), while anti-HIV was negative.
Bone marrow aspiration revealed no evidence of hematological malignancy.
Although the CD18 expression study remains unavailable at our institution, our patients were suspected of having LAD-1^0 due to the early age of onset[3,7-9].

segregation.statement: Both parents heterozygous for both variants (unaffected status implied by 'carrier', not described). An unaffected sister was not reported as tested.

Mutations were also characterized by the heterozygous state in both parents of P1 and P2, suggesting carrier status in the parents (Figure 2).
His sister had no health issues despite being the second child of consanguineous parents.

concerns: The paper contradicts itself on the base change: Results, Figure 2 and Tables give c.920T>C, but the Abstract and Discussion write c.920C>T. Both give p.Leu307Pro; the batch uses c.920T>C.

P1 is also homozygous for a second ITGB2 missense variant, c.758G>A (p.Arg253His); the authors' Table 1 lists a dbSNP/ClinVar entry (rs200423927) and an ExAC heterozygous frequency (0.0002817) for it. Either variant, or both, could explain the phenotype; they cannot be separated by segregation in this family.
No CD18 flow cytometry was done, so the LAD-I diagnosis rests on clinical features and sequencing.
notes_for_panel: Single Thai case report (P1, Burmese boy, consanguineous parents). Homozygous for both c.920T>C and c.758G>A; both parents heterozygous for both. No CD18 study, no functional study.
